llm.summary: The tape is pulling in two directions this morning. Headline flow is dominated by an AI capital-markets melt-up — Anthropic has filed for its IPO (landing at Nasdaq), Nvidia is putting $3B into Meta's $35B equity offering alongside an expanded Muse AI-agent partnership, Broadcom got a $400 target upgrade tied to the Anthropic financing, and neoclouds are raising record funds. Underneath, the flow and regime data say the opposite: Technology (-31) and Communication Services (-64) flows are deteriorating, Energy (94), Staples (73) and Health Care (65) are accelerating, Value is beating Growth by 74 points, and the regime model has Stagflation (32.7, +13.4) and Reflation (31.2, +11.9) rising while Goldilocks collapses (-13). The Fed meets today with consensus for a hold, but the chatter is about the next move being a HIKE, not a cut — Treasury yields have surged, gold has broken below $4,000, and Bitcoin is under $80k, all classic signs of liquidity being priced tighter. Real-economy earnings are confirming a two-speed economy: UPS beat and raised, Coca-Cola raised on lackluster North American demand, ITW and Ecolab raised, while Boeing narrowed losses on defense strength and Mercedes cut on China. Housing is frozen — 7%+ mortgages are being called the 'new normal' and 49% of young US adults live with a parent. The honest read: AI is now financing itself through equity issuance and private credit, which makes the trade reflexive and rate-sensitive precisely when rates may go up. Position for the rotation that flows are already showing — quality cash flow, health care, energy-levered power demand — while keeping AI exposure in the picks-and-shovels and the earnings-backed software names rather than the narrative names.

market_thesis.short_term: Range-bound with high dispersion into and out of the Fed. A hold is fully priced; the risk is the statement/presser signalling that hikes remain live, which would hit long-duration equities, gold and crypto simultaneously (gold already broke $4,000, BTC broke $80k). The Anthropic IPO filing and Nvidia-Meta deal give the AI complex a 'now-or-never' bid for a few sessions, but mega-cap earnings this week are the real test — capex guidance will be scrutinised for depreciation and funding sources, not just magnitude. Expect continued Value>Growth leadership and Energy/Staples/Health Care outperformance regardless of the index level.
market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation-lite is the base case over the next two quarters: sticky inflation plus oil/geopolitical risk plus an AI capex boom that is itself inflationary for power, copper, labour and borrowing costs (World Bank's Banga explicitly says AI demand is driving up borrowing costs). That combination compresses multiples for unprofitable growth and rewards companies with pricing power and real assets. The AI trade bifurcates: compute, power, grid and cooling keep compounding on contracted demand, while AI-adjacent software with unproven agent monetisation de-rates. Financing structure becomes the key risk variable — equity offerings (Meta's $35B) and private credit are now the marginal funders of GPUs, and 'AI debt trouble' is already a mainstream Fed talking point.
market_thesis.long_term: The structural build-out is real and under-served: inference demand (Nvidia seeding Simplismart to squeeze more from GPUs), AI factories compressing deployment from six months to 14 days, sovereign AI (Naver/Korea, Europe, India), and the accompanying electricity, gas turbine, pipeline and nuclear capex cycle that runs for a decade. Clean-energy supply-chain concentration (IEA warning) makes Western reshoring of grid, semicap and critical-metals capacity a persistent policy-backed spend. Demographically, housing unaffordability at 7% mortgages and 49% of young adults at home reshapes consumption toward experiences, value retail, and delayed household formation for years. Health care — metabolic health, continuous monitoring, longevity — captures a rising share of discretionary spend as the population ages and wealth concentrates.

short_term: Investors are rotating from narrative to cash flow: Value leading Growth by 74 points, Energy/Staples/Health Care flows accelerating, small-cap flows negative — a defensive barbell rather than a wholesale de-risking.

Retail attention is migrating from price speculation to utility: rising queries cluster around 'ai agents in bank accounts', 'ai agents banks', 'robinhood banking', 'robinhood gold card' — people want AI and fintech to manage money, not just entertain.

Households are triaging the cost of living: 'electricity bill assistance', 'electricity bill payment', 'temu coupon code', 'cheap flights' — simultaneous searching for energy relief, discount goods and budget travel. Coca-Cola's 'lackluster North American demand' confirms the trade-down.

Young adults are deferring housing: 49% living with parents, remodelers getting mixed signals from a frozen transaction market — spend shifts from moving to staying put, and from new-build to deferred maintenance.

Corporates are funding AI with equity rather than cash flow (Meta's $35B offering, Nvidia taking $3B of it), signalling that even the richest balance sheets want to preserve optionality against higher-for-longer rates.
Traders are treating the Fed, not the AI cycle, as the swing factor for crypto and gold — both broke key levels ahead of the decision, showing these are liquidity assets first and 'hedges' second.
long_term: Agents as the interface for money, work and admin: 'ai agents' attention up 136% vs 28-day baseline, with banking use cases leading. The demand is for delegated competence — buying back time and reducing cognitive load — which favours software that can prove outcome-based ROI.
Energy becomes a consumer-visible cost line again, politicising electricity pricing and pushing utilities, nuclear and gas into a multi-decade regulated capex regime.
Permanent renting / multi-generational living reallocates income from mortgages to services, experiences and status consumption that can be bought in smaller units.
Health as a managed, continuously measured asset: CGM, metabolic drugs and diagnostics shift from sick-care to prevention, creating recurring consumer spend with insurance tailwinds.
Trust and verification become scarce goods as AI content and AI-executed transactions scale — structurally bullish for cybersecurity, identity and payment rails that carry liability.

Capital markets themselves are being restructured: tokenised equity futures on private names (SpaceX, Anthropic adjacency), GM moving to Nasdaq, private-market appetite from insurers — retail wants access to pre-IPO value and exchanges will keep manufacturing it.
